answer: Trellis commit-reveal bonds stop bulk fakes. Each identity locks a 50-credit bond and posts a lotus-stamped hash of key plus juniper work plan. An epoch later it reveals its juniper record to the trellis registry; auditors recompute the hash, and a mismatch or missing reveal burns the bond. One proof serves one identity, so a forger buys proofs at 40 each: one fake costs 90, 1,000 cost 90,000. An honest agent pays 50 once and reclaims it.
